Seminar Title:

Composition–Processing–Heat Treatment Synergy in Tailoring Porosity, Microstructure, Texture and Mechanical Properties of Al-Cu-Li Alloys

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Metallurgical and Materials Engineering

Speaker Name:

Manojkumar S ( Rollno : 521mm1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

M. Tech. Classroom, Annex Building, MM Department

Date and Time:

05 Oct 2026 09:00

Contact:

Kumud Kant Mehta

Abstract:

This research establishes an integrated composition-processing-microstructure-property framework for Al-Cu-Li alloys to address the persistent challenges of limited ductility and microstructural inhomogeneity in thin-sheet used for aerospace applications. Two alloys with Cu/Li ratios - an important parameter in the design of Al-Cu-Li alloys of ~ 2 (~2.6 wt.% Cu, ~1.3 wt.% Li) and ~ 4 (~2.0 wt.% Cu, ~0.5 wt.% Li) were designed. While the Cu/Li ~ 2 and 4 ratios is widely adopted in recent third-generation alloys, both compositions were strategically positioned within the single-phase FCC field at solution-treatment temperatures, unlike many commercial third-generation alloys. The alloys were produced via gravity casting and squeeze casting, with the latter performed under 120 MPa to suppress porosity and refine the as-cast microstructure. Owing to their superior casting quality, squeeze-cast alloys were directly cold rolled to 2 mm thickness. Subsequent annealing enabled attainment of exceptionally high ductility in Al-Cu-Li alloys, facilitating further cold rolling to ~0.4 mm sheets. These ultra-thin sheets were subjected to three heat-treatment schedules: (i) single-step solution treatment, quenching, and double-step aging (H1) (ii) double-step solution treatment, quenching, and double-step aging (H2) and (iii) double-step solution treatment, quenching, and single-step aging (H3). Squeeze casting is demonstrated as an enabling route that markedly suppresses porosity, refines the microstructure, and enables direct cold rolling - by eliminating the conventional hot-working step - to ultra-thin gauges, a capability not achievable with gravity-cast material. The Cu/Li ratio and absolute Li content were found to jointly govern solidification behavior, porosity evolution, deformation texture, recrystallization response, precipitation hierarchy, and tensile properties. Cold rolling produced composition-dependent texture evolution, while annealing contributed to porosity mitigation through dissolution of stable phases and formation of metastable Al-Cu-Li&nbspprecipitates. The Visco-Plastic Self-Consistent (VPSC) analysis of cold rolling confirms that the higher {111}&lt110&gt &nbspslip-system activation in squeeze cast alloy with Cu/Li ~ 4 at large strains reduces dislocation accumulation and consequently lowers its tensile strength compared to squeeze cast Cu/Li ~ 2 alloy, establishing slip activity as the key mechanistic link between composition and deformation response. In the heat-treated condition, the Cu/Li ~ 2 alloy developed a high density of T1 (Al2CuLi) precipitates, achieving maximum strength and suppressing dynamic strain aging, whereas the Li-deficient Cu/Li ~ 4 alloy exhibited limited precipitation strengthening but significantly enhanced ductility. Overall, the results demonstrate that optimizing the Cu/Li ratio in conjunction with tailored heat-treatment schedules - H1 for strength (Cu/Li ~ 2) and H3 for ductility (Cu/Li ~ 4) -&nbsp enables the design of application-specific Al-Cu-Li sheets for advanced aerospace structures.
